Matching: lint name + object identity (functions: name(arguments); tables: table name). INFO-level findings never fail regardless of this file. mode=accepted -> finding is expected, never fails, never files; mode=tracked -> finding is known and owned by tracked_in, never fails, not re-filed; removing a rule makes its findings live again.

rules.reason:
RLS helper + intentional client-RPC class. These MUST stay executable by authenticated: RLS policies evaluate the helpers in the caller's context, and a prior revoke pass broke production RLS (see crm7 20260521024707/20260527022039 hotfix_restore_rls_helper_grants history). Operator directive 2026-06-11: do NOT blanket-fail this class until replaced by a proven alternative. A SECURITY DEFINER function NOT on this list IS a failure - the list is exhaustive, not a category waiver. Added 2026-08-06: the three bulk_data_* entry points and is_gto_admin(p_tenant_id uuid). The bulk RPCs are the /settings/data API and MUST stay client-callable; what makes them safe is their own gates — a membership guard against auth_tenant_id() before any table is touched, an is_pii/min_role field gate at every admission point, and RLS on every base table underneath. Their seven INTERNAL _bulk_data_* helpers are NOT here: crm7 migration 20260806350000 revokes EXECUTE from anon/authenticated on those, so only the entry points remain reachable. is_gto_admin(p_tenant_id uuid) is an RLS helper of the same class as is_gto_staff(uuid) and auth_tenant_id() already in this list.

ADDED 2026-08-11 — the R8 quote handoff (crm7#1604, crm7#1570). The operator ruled that R8 must have a real transport rather than a paste-a-JSON box: 'well it should have the transport.'

NOTE WHAT IS DIFFERENT ABOUT THESE THREE: they are NOT anon-reachable, unlike every other token pair in this estate. R8 mints from the browser using its own already-authenticated Supabase session against the same project, so both RPCs require `authenticated` and anon is revoked by name. There is no shared secret for a SPA to leak in a bundle, and no anonymous surface at all. That is why they sit in this rule and not the anon one.

SECURITY DEFINER is the mechanism: the token table has no SELECT policy for anyone, so the hash is unreadable from the client by construction. Tokens are stored hashed, are single-use, expire in 15 minutes, and minting is rate-limited to 20/hour/user.

Verified by pgTAP suite 74, plan(30), 30/30 — positively controlled, including a valid token redeemed by a DIFFERENT authenticated user than the minter with the payload round-tripping byte-for-byte, and the 21st mint in an hour refused. The anon-revocation assertion is catalog-based rather than a live probe: a runtime probe of the revoked function crashed local Postgres outright, reproducing the hazard documented in crm7#773.

ADDED 2026-08-11 — five functions that were APPLIED TO PRODUCTION on 2026-08-10 and never allowlisted. My omission: both authoring lanes reported the exact signatures and were correctly told not to edit this file themselves, and I did not add them. The sweep has been red since the promotion, and the sweep was right.

  portal_invite_mint / portal_invite_accept (crm7#1558) — the portal invite. mint is staff-only, gated on check_user_portal_role(auth.uid(), tenant, owner|admin), returns the raw token once and stores only a hash. accept requires an authenticated caller and returns NULL for every refusal rather than raising, deliberately: it records a rate-limit attempt before it knows the outcome, and a RAISE would roll back that same counter. Also non-enumerating. 37 pgTAP assertions.

  resolve_enterprise_root_id / employers_set_enterprise_root_id / tenants_recompute_employer_roots_on_reparent (crm7#1554) — the enterprise-root machinery behind the ABN uniqueness scope. Two are trigger functions, not client-callable surfaces; resolve_enterprise_root_id walks tenants.parent_tenant_id using tenant_subtree_ids(), the only cycle-safe walker of the four. All three pin search_path and revoke anon by name.

ADDED 2026-08-18 — can_write_role_capability(p_tenant_id uuid, p_capability text). It is an RLS helper of exactly the class this rule exists for: the three role_capabilities_admin_{insert,update,delete} policies call it in their USING/WITH CHECK clauses, and a policy expression is evaluated as the CALLING role — so revoking EXECUTE from authenticated would not harden anything, it would break every admin write to role_capabilities. SECURITY DEFINER is load-bearing for the reason the function's own header states: an INVOKER version recurses through user_tenants' RLS.
What makes a direct RPC call safe is that the function answers only about the CALLER — its membership limb is pinned to auth.uid(), so a signed-in user can learn whether THEY may write a capability, which they can already establish by attempting the write. It returns no row data and takes no user_id parameter, so it cannot be aimed at another account.
Verified live 2026-08-18: capability_catalogue, the only table it reads, has RLS enabled with one policy; anon holds no SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and authenticated is read-only.
rules.review: Re-justify before adding any new function; shrink the list as helpers migrate to SECURITY INVOKER or out of the exposed schema. 2026-08-24: sync_people_assigned_field_officer() was REMOVED rather than added — a trigger function needs no EXECUTE grant, proven by firing it with the grant revoked. 2026-08-31: rename_physical_column and reorder_entity_fields ADDED, each with the deployed function's own gating measured rather than asserted — see their notes. rename_physical_column ships with an EMPTY allowlist, so it is inert on arrival.

notes.is_platform_developer(): RLS/authorization helper. SECURITY DEFINER so a policy can evaluate it without the caller holding read access to profiles. Returns a boolean only; leaks nothing about other users. Deliberately narrower than is_platform_super_admin() (developer ONLY, excludes tester).
notes.schema_authority_tenant_ids(): RLS helper on tenant_schema_layout. SECURITY DEFINER so the policy can read user_tenants/tenants without granting the caller access to them. Returns only tenant ids the caller already has authority over; while acting-as it NARROWS to that subtree rather than widening.
notes.tenant_subtree_ids(root_tenant_id uuid): Recursive parent_tenant_id walk used by the above. Depth-capped at 10. Takes a tenant id the caller must already be authorized for; returns ids only, no row data.
notes.update_platform_entity_label(p_entity_id: INTENTIONAL privileged write path, not a helper. It is the ONLY app-level route to a platform-owned tenant_entities row (RLS denies those rows to every user by design). SECURITY DEFINER IS the mechanism; the is_platform_developer() check inside it is the authorization. Restricted to label/description, refuses tenant-owned rows so it cannot become an RLS bypass, and every call is written to platform_schema_audit. Verified live 2026-08-06: a tester and a plain user both get 42501.
notes.acting_tenant_id(): RLS helper. Returns the tenant a platform super admin is currently acting as, or nothing. SECURITY DEFINER so policies can read platform_admin_acting_as without granting callers access to it. Gated on is_platform_super_admin() AND expires_at > now(), so a lapsed or unauthorized session yields no rows.
notes.is_platform_super_admin(): RLS helper. Boolean only. SECURITY DEFINER so a policy can read profiles without the caller holding access. Admits developer | platform_admin | is_super_admin — the act-as set. Deliberately WIDER than is_platform_developer(), which alone gates platform schema writes.
notes.platform_admin_act_as(target_tenant_id u: INTENTIONAL privileged write, not a helper. Starts an acting-as session; SECURITY DEFINER IS the mechanism because platform_admin_acting_as has no write policies at all. Authorization is the is_platform_super_admin() check inside it, the target tenant must exist, and every start is written to platform_admin_act_as_audit. Sessions carry a hard 12h expires_at.
notes.platform_admin_stop_acting(): Counterpart to the above; clears the caller's own acting-as row and audits the stop. SECURITY DEFINER for the same reason. Acts only on auth.uid()'s own row.
notes.report_catalog_approve_entity(p_key text: INTENTIONAL privileged write path, not a helper — same class as update_platform_entity_label. It is the developer-approval step of the D3 promotion path (schema-builder entity -> DRAFT catalog row -> developer approves -> active), so it MUST be client-callable: an RPC has to be reachable in order to return its denial. SECURITY DEFINER is the mechanism; the is_platform_developer() check inside it is the authorization. anon is already REVOKED (verified live: has_function_privilege('anon',...) = false). Verified live 2026-08-07 inside a guaranteed rollback: a non-developer (owner of Lookn, platform_role='user') calling it is DENIED with 'only a platform developer may approve a proposed entity into the catalog'. Added by the supervisor lane while unblocking bsuite#1796; the implementing lane owns the function.
notes.migration_high_water_mark():
INTENTIONAL client-readable surface, and the authenticated grant IS the feature. It exposes the APPLIED-migration high-water mark to the Settings -> System Information panel so a signed-in user can tell 'merged but not applied' apart from a defect. There is ONE Supabase project: d.crm.crm7.app serves `development` CODE against a `main`-STATE database, and the applier runs on main only, so a merged, correct, migration-dependent feature renders EMPTY on dev with nothing in the app distinguishing that from a bug. The CODE half of the comparison (__BUILD_COMMIT__) was already in the browser; this is the DATABASE half. Revoking it does not harden anything, it deletes the feature.

SECURITY DEFINER is the only route, verified live rather than assumed: supabase_migrations has nspacl = NULL and the ledger table relacl = NULL, so NO PostgREST role reaches it -- service_role included. A SECURITY INVOKER function would return nothing, and granting direct SELECT would hand callers statements[] and rollback[], i.e. the full DDL of every migration.

WHAT LEAVES THE SCHEMA IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT, and it is narrow by construction: the return type is TABLE(high_water_mark text, applied_count bigint) and the body selects only max(version) and count(*). Verified live 2026-08-17: returns ('20260821010000', 703). No statements[] or rollback[] is reachable through it.

anon is already revoked BY NAME -- confirmed live, has_function_privilege('anon', ...) = false, ACL {postgres=X, service_role=X, authenticated=X}. Both revoke routes matter here: a postgres-created function arrives with a built-in EXECUTE TO PUBLIC that ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES does not remove, so REVOKE FROM PUBLIC and REVOKE FROM anon are not substitutes for one another.
notes.platform_oauth_clients():
INTENTIONAL privileged READ path, and the authenticated grant IS the feature. It is the only route to the OAuth client registry for the Developer Portal, replacing a HARDCODED list of five clients that was duplicated across two pages and had already drifted from reality (real names 'R8' vs the literal's 'R8 Calculator'/'R80.4'; real hosts www.crm7.app and r8-c.vercel.app vs the literal's crm.crm7.app and r8.crm7.app). All five hardcoded ids were real and none soft-deleted, so the defect was asserted status and drift, not invented rows.

SECURITY DEFINER is the mechanism: auth.oauth_clients is not readable by any PostgREST role, so a SECURITY INVOKER function would return nothing. The authorization is the gate INSIDE the function, which mirrors canUsePlatformKit exactly — platform_role IN ('platform_admin','developer'). Deliberately NOT is_platform_developer(), which is developer-only and would lock out platform_admin, making the page gate and the data source disagree; that mismatch is exactly the RC2 class this estate has already been bitten by.

WHAT LEAVES THE FUNCTION IS THE ARGUMENT: identity metadata only. It never returns client_secret_hash, grant_types or token_endpoint_auth_method. And it RAISES SQLSTATE 42501 on refusal rather than filtering to zero rows — a refusal that returns an empty set is indistinguishable from an empty registry, which would read as 'no OAuth clients exist' to an unauthorised viewer.

anon is revoked BY NAME and via PUBLIC, then the ACL is asserted back in a DO block that RAISEs. Both revoke routes are needed and neither covers the other.
notes.clone_tenant_role(p_source_role_id uuid,: Writes tenant_roles + role_capabilities. SECURITY DEFINER because INVOKER cannot read a PLATFORM source role's grants through RLS. It checks its own authority against schema_authority_tenant_ids() before writing, so the grant does not decide who may call it — the body does.
notes.current_user_has_capability(p_tenant_id: Self-scoped: it passes auth.uid() and cannot be asked about anyone else. The subject is not a parameter, so there is nothing for a caller to point elsewhere.
notes.is_field_manager(p_tenant_id uuid): Takes only a tenant and answers about the CALLER. Returns a boolean; reveals nothing about any other user.
notes.effective_user_capabilities(p_user_id uu: Arbitrary subject, so the grant alone was NOT sufficient — until 20260906000000 any signed-in user could resolve any user's capabilities in any tenant, which is cross-tenant disclosure of who can do what. The right to ASK is now checked by caller_may_read_capabilities_of() (self, tenant owner/admin, or platform developer), which is SECURITY INVOKER so it answers for the caller. Fails closed as zero rows. Stays executable because BSU's permissions editor (src/lib/admin/userCapabilityOverrides.ts) legitimately resolves ANOTHER user for a tenant admin; revoking would close the hole by breaking the feature.
notes.user_has_capability(p_user_id uuid, p_te: Thin wrapper over effective_user_capabilities() and inherits its caller check, so the same reasoning applies. Kept SECURITY DEFINER so 20260905000000's fail-closed boolean contract holds: it answers a boolean question with a boolean rather than a NOT FOUND callers must interpret.
notes.reorder_entity_fields(p_entity_id uuid,: Schema Builder client RPC. SECURITY DEFINER so one caller can rewrite every tenant_field_definitions.sort_order for an entity atomically — INVOKER cannot hold that row set stable under RLS, and a partial reorder leaves duplicate or gapped sort_order the UI reads as lost fields. Measured on the deployed function 2026-08-31: reads auth.uid(), checks user_tenants membership, raises on failure. anon is NOT granted. Called by SchemaCanvas, which crm7 (1 site) and BSU (3 sites) render, so authenticated EXECUTE is the intended reach.
notes.rename_physical_column(p_entity_id uuid,: Schema Builder client RPC. SECURITY DEFINER because it runs ALTER TABLE ... RENAME COLUMN, which INVOKER cannot do under RLS-scoped roles. This is the hardened replacement for the privilege-escalation shape: the previous version took its ALTER target from caller-controlled tenant_entities.name, so any tenant admin could rename a column on any public table including user_tenants.role. Measured on the deployed function 2026-08-31: constrained by the schema_builder_physical_tables allowlist (which ships EMPTY, so the RPC is inert until a table is explicitly opted in), reads auth.uid(), checks user_tenants membership, raises on failure, and writes every attempt to schema_mutations_audit. anon is NOT granted.

rules.reason: INFO-level operator-side Auth pool sizing; relevant only at instance scale-up.

conduit#229 talent-community consent RPCs. r7_issue_talent_pool_consent_token mints a single-use token (re-checks caller tenant membership when auth.uid() is non-null); r7_redeem_talent_pool_consent validates a SHA-256-hashed single-use 30-day token and sets consent. SECURITY DEFINER is required to write across tenant RLS with token-gated authz inside the function. Intentional, live-verified on prod 2026-06-24.

conduit#229 public talent-community opt-in. r7_redeem_talent_pool_consent is the ONLY anon-reachable write in conduit by design: it is token-gated (32-byte raw token, SHA-256 hash compare), single-use, 30-day expiry, non-enumerating, returns no PII. Equivalent to a magic-link. Live-verified on prod 2026-06-24 (consent flip + token consumed).

2026-07-02 Qodo-fix RPCs. search_profiles_by_name: throughput team-member selector — profiles RLS is self-only, so a narrow SECDEF search returning ONLY (id, full_name, company), auth-required, pinned search_path (throughput PR#232 finding 1). r7_submit_public_application: conduit public apply handler — replaced four unsafe anon INSERT policies with one fail-closed SECDEF entrypoint (rate-limited 3/hr rolling window per IP/job, consent-gated sensitive demographics, tenant derived from the job row); authenticated grant is transitive via anon->authenticated inheritance of the public apply path (conduit PR#348 findings 2-4). SIGNATURE CHANGED 2026-08-12 (conduit#433 / conduit#434, applied to production the same day): p_ip_hash moved from position 2 to LAST and gained a DEFAULT — the expand step of Expand->Migrate->Contract, so the old and new browser call shapes both resolve. The function no longer reads x-forwarded-for at all; the throttle keys on cf-connecting-ip, which Cloudflare rejects when a client supplies it (verified empirically, not from documentation: a spoofed header returns Cloudflare error code 1000 before reaching PostgREST). Entries are REPLACED, not added alongside — the pre-fix signature no longer exists in production (one overload, confirmed via to_regprocedure), and carrying a dead entry is exactly the stale-waiver problem this file's own tooling now self-reports. Contraction tracked at conduit#435. CONTRACTION APPLIED: conduit migration 20261203000000 (conduit#435 contract step) drops p_ip_hash; entry updated to the post-contract 25-arg signature. Old signature replaced, not kept alongside, per this file's stale-waiver rule. NOTE: both the 26-arg (live, pre-contract) and 25-arg (post-contract) signatures are carried while conduit 20261203000000 remains pending; drop the 26-arg entry once it applies.

rules.reason:
Charge-rate-quote signing workflow — anon-reachable BY DESIGN for external signers (host employers, site contacts) who may not have authenticated sessions. Token-gated: validates p_token is a valid signing token, enforces signing context, logs audit trail. Fail-closed SECDEF ensures signing operations work across tenant boundaries. Applied 2026-07-06.

ADDED 2026-08-11 — the host agreement signing pair, crm7#1594. Same shape and same justification as the charge-rate quote pair above, because it is deliberately the same mechanism generalised rather than a second one: the operator ruled that host agreements are generated by the GTO in CRM7 and issued for e-signing (bsuite#1885), and the quote path was already doing exactly that job for an external party with no login.

ANON-REACHABLE BY NECESSITY. The signer is a host employer representative who has no account and never will — requiring one would mean asking every host to register before they can sign an agreement. get_host_agreement_signing_context reads only what the signing page must render; redeem_host_agreement_signature is the only write path.

FAIL-CLOSED REGARDLESS OF THE GRANT: the token is stored as a HASH and never in the clear, is single-use, expires, and is rate-limited. anon cannot read the hash table at all. Verified by pgTAP suite 69 with plan(47), 47/47 passing — and positively controlled in both directions, including the successful redemption executed AS anon rather than in role-neutral SQL, because a refusal-only test cannot distinguish a working gate from a dead endpoint.

Joins the four endpoints tracked on bsuite#1869; the expiry and rate-limiting review asked for there covers these two as well.

ADDED 2026-08-11 — portal_invite_accept(p_token text), applied 2026-08-10 and not allowlisted at the time. It is anon-reachable by necessity: the invitee clicks a link with no session. It refuses immediately when auth.uid() IS NULL, checked BEFORE the token is read so an anonymous caller cannot use it to discover which tokens exist, and it returns NULL for every refusal rather than raising.

rules.reason:
The seventeen SECURITY DEFINER functions that arrived with the 2026-08-09 promotion (bsuite#1845): the T4 data-grant machinery (crm7#1481, migrations 20260809030000 / 20260809060000), the payroll vault RPCs (20260808160000), the remittance stamp (20260808190000) and the onboarding block override. Enumerated function-by-function per the standing rule that this list is exhaustive, not a category waiver.

VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-10 against the production catalog, for all seventeen:
  * SECURITY DEFINER with search_path pinned to 'public, pg_temp' — all 17.
  * has_function_privilege('anon', ...) = FALSE — all 17. None is reachable unauthenticated.

They fall into two classes.

(1) RLS PREDICATES, the established accepted class. data_grant_entity_permitted, data_grant_field_permitted, data_grant_row_permit, data_grant_table_row_permit, data_grant_widest, data_grantor_accessible_field_ids, data_grantor_is_tier_holder, data_is_grant_restricted, person_ids_for_current_user. These are evaluated INSIDE RLS policies, so they must be executable by the querying role — that is the same reason auth_tenant_id() and is_gto_admin() are already on this list. They return booleans or id lists and expose no row data. SECURITY DEFINER is required so a policy can consult the grant tables without granting the caller read access to them.

(2) INTENTIONAL PRIVILEGED WRITE/READ PATHS, where SECURITY DEFINER IS the mechanism and an explicit check inside the function IS the authorization — the same shape as update_platform_entity_label and the bulk_data_* entry points already accepted. Each was read and its gate confirmed, not assumed:
  - data_grant_create / data_create_restricted_user: thin wrappers over _data_grant_insert, which is NOT executable by authenticated or anon (verified) and whose FIRST statement raises 42501 unless data_grantor_is_tier_holder(p_tenant_id). It further refuses an unknown entity, an entity absent from data_grant_enabled_entities, and a NULL/empty field list — 'all fields' as a wildcard is rejected outright.
  - data_grant_revoke: checks auth.uid() and raises.
  - save_person_bank_account / save_person_tax_declaration: gate on check_user_portal_role(auth.uid(), tenant, ['owner','admin']) OR the person themselves. The function carries its own comment saying authorization is checked there precisely BECAUSE SECURITY DEFINER bypasses the RLS that would otherwise do it.
  - person_bank_accounts_for_payment: requires owner/admin on the tenant of EVERY person id passed, and refuses the whole call if any one is outside — deliberately, because a partial payment file is worse than a refused one.
  - record_onboarding_block_override: owner/admin/manager on the person's tenant, and validates the consequence enum.
  - record_payroll_remittance_stamp: checks auth.uid() and raises.

WHY THIS ENTRY EXISTS RATHER THAN A GREEN JOB: the sweep was RED from 2026-08-09 21:09 because these seventeen were new and unallowlisted. That is the gate working exactly as designed — a new SECURITY DEFINER function exposed to authenticated MUST fail until a human has justified it. This is that justification.
rules.review: Re-justify if any signature changes — the objects are matched by full signature, so an added parameter creates a NEW unallowlisted finding and correctly re-fails the sweep. Revisit the two payroll writers when the runtime defects noted on bsuite#1845 are fixed (editing a bank account erases the prior verification event; re-saving a tax declaration supersedes a signed one with an unsigned one).

notes.data_grant_create(...): Not a helper — the privileged creation path for a restricted-guest grant. Safe because the real work sits in _data_grant_insert, which authenticated cannot call, and which refuses anyone who is not a tier-holder (platform developer, tenant gto_admin, or tenant owner) with 42501.
notes.person_bank_accounts_for_payment(p_perso: Reads bank details for a payment run and triggers account-number decryption, so it is the highest-value function in this set. All-or-nothing tenant check: owner/admin on every person's tenant, else the entire call is refused. Every decryption is written to payroll_secret_access_log.
notes.save_person_tax_declaration(...): Writes a tax file number. Gated on owner/admin of the person's tenant, or the person themselves. Known runtime defect, tracked on bsuite#1845 rather than here: re-saving to correct one field supersedes a signed declaration with an unsigned one because the signature date is not carried forward. That is a procedure defect, not a privilege defect — it does not change who may call this.
notes.person_ids_for_current_user(): RLS/self-service helper. Returns only the person rows linked to auth.uid(); no arguments, so it cannot be pointed at anyone else.

rules.reason:
Arrived with the 2026-08-16 P0 sweep (crm7#1749, migration 20260820120000), which moved email integration credentials out of PLAINTEXT `imap_password`/`smtp_password` columns and into Vault, then DROPPED those columns. This RPC is the write half of that move, and `authenticated` EXECUTE is the mechanism, not an oversight: a tenant user connecting their own mailbox must be able to store the credential, and SECURITY DEFINER is required because the caller must NOT be able to read or write `vault.secrets` directly.

VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-16 against the production catalog, not assumed:
  * SECURITY DEFINER with search_path pinned to 'public, pg_temp'.
  * has_function_privilege('anon', ...) = FALSE. Not reachable unauthenticated.
  * ACL is exactly postgres=X | service_role=X | authenticated=X — the same shape every other RLS/vault helper in this estate carries.

Its gate was read line by line rather than presumed. Four checks, in order, each raising rather than returning:
  1. `p_token_field` must be one of access_token / refresh_token / smtp_password / imap_password. This is checked BEFORE the value is used to build the target column name via format('%I'), so the identifier is never attacker-controlled — the validation is what makes the dynamic UPDATE safe, and it is first for that reason.
  2. auth.uid() must be non-null.
  3. The secret must be non-empty.
  4. The caller must hold owner/admin/manager/staff in the INTEGRATION'S OWN tenant, via auth_tenant_id_with_role — the same role list as the table's own tenant_insert/update/delete_email_integrations policies (20260706120000). A missing row and a wrong-tenant row raise the SAME message, so the function cannot be used to probe which integration ids exist.

It writes ONLY the `*_vault_id` pointer column back onto the row and returns the vault id. It never returns the secret, and there is no read counterpart here — decryption stays behind the pre-existing `email_integration_get_decrypted_token`, whose grants this change left untouched (asserted as a control in the migration's dry-run).

WHY THIS ENTRY EXISTS RATHER THAN A GREEN JOB: the sweep passed on `development` at 10:33 and failed at 11:35 once the applier had run this migration. That is the gate working exactly as designed — a new SECURITY DEFINER function exposed to authenticated MUST fail until a human has justified it. This is that justification.
rules.review: Re-justify if the signature changes — objects are matched by full signature, so an added parameter creates a NEW unallowlisted finding and correctly re-fails the sweep. Also re-justify if the p_token_field allow-list is ever widened: that list is what makes the dynamic format('%I') UPDATE safe.

Mailbox P0 (BSU#1105/#1108/#1110). Both are browser-called SECURITY DEFINER RPCs because the row's own RLS cannot reach vault.secrets, and a PostgREST DELETE that matches zero rows returns success. authenticated EXECUTE is the mechanism: a person confirming or disconnecting THEIR mailbox must be able to call them; anon is revoked.

rules.reason:
The two RLS helpers introduced by crm7#1751 (migration 20260820130000), which gave contacts_select a host-employer limb and closed the confirmed cross-tenant enumeration exposure in crm7#1729 / #1675.

These are the ESTABLISHED ACCEPTED CLASS already described on the 2026-08-10 entry above: RLS PREDICATES. They are evaluated INSIDE a policy, so they must be executable by the querying role — the identical reason auth_tenant_id(), is_gto_admin() and the nine data_grant_* predicates are already on this list. Revoking EXECUTE from authenticated would not narrow contacts reads; it would fail every one of them. SECURITY DEFINER is required so a policy can consult org_members without granting the caller read access to it.

VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-16 against the production catalog, both functions:
  * SECURITY DEFINER with search_path pinned to 'public, pg_temp'.
  * has_function_privilege('anon', ...) = FALSE. Neither is reachable unauthenticated.
  * Each is referenced by exactly ONE policy (contacts_select) — no wider blast radius.

Neither exposes row data. is_host_supervisor_of_tenant returns a BOOLEAN — whether the caller holds gto_role='host_supervisor' in the tenant passed. get_host_employer_id_for_tenant returns a single UUID — the caller's OWN host employer for that tenant, and only for a caller who is a host supervisor there. Neither takes a user id, so neither can be pointed at anyone else: both key off auth.uid() internally.

WHY THE SECOND ONE EXISTS AT ALL, since it duplicates get_user_host_employer_id(): that older helper takes no tenant and ends in a bare LIMIT 1. Harmless in the six ADDITIVE policies already using it, because they only widen. In contacts_select it became the SOLE clause deciding a host supervisor's reads, so the arbitrary pick became an authorization decision — measured, it reached 4 rows of a tenant the caller had no membership in. The tenant-scoped, ORDER BY-deterministic replacement is what closed that.
rules.review: Re-justify if either signature changes — objects match by full signature. Also re-justify if either is ever called from a policy other than contacts_select: the 'one policy, no wider blast radius' claim above is part of why they are accepted rather than tracked.

rules.why: The R8 quote-return handoff. Both write r8_quote_return_tickets, which has RLS enabled and zero policies by design, so an INVOKER function could not touch the row at all. Read in full on 2026-08-26 rather than accepted on their annotations. mint() takes a caller-supplied placement id -- the IDOR shape -- and closes it: the tenant is read off the placement ROW after proving membership via auth_tenant_id_with_role, using IN (SELECT ...) because that helper RETURNS SETOF and a scalar would silently compare whichever membership came back first; the not-found reply is constant and reveals nothing the caller did not supply. redeem() takes only an opaque token, rate-limits with an atomic upsert where the increment IS the check, refuses by RETURNING rather than RAISING so the counter survives the refusal, locks the ticket FOR UPDATE against a concurrent double-redeem, and treats the tenant as a property of the TICKET -- a wrong-tenant holder gets the identical 'invalid_or_expired' message, so trying is not a tenant oracle.

rules.reason: is_developer_admin() is an RLS helper of exactly the class the first rule in this file exists for, and it is here because the advisor sweep went red on it and the sweep was right to: it was not allowlisted. WHY EXECUTE CANNOT SIMPLY BE REVOKED. Four policies call it -- "Admins manage applications", "Admins manage page_sections", "Admins manage services", "Admins manage site_metadata", all FOR ALL to authenticated on the braden CMS tables. A policy expression is evaluated as the CALLING role, so revoking EXECUTE from authenticated would not harden anything; it would break every admin write to those four tables. That is not a prediction: this estate already did it once, and the first rule in this file records the hotfix history (crm7 20260521024707 / 20260527022039). objects: workflow_run_step_complete(p_step_id uuid, p_outcome text, p_error text)
rules.reason: Phase 3 workflow execution bridge (20261104000000). This is the ONE function of the eight the bridge adds that authenticated may execute, and that is the design rather than an oversight: workflow_run_advance, workflow_run_activate_node, workflow_emit_event and workflow_advance_on_queue_settled are all SECURITY DEFINER with NO execute grant to authenticated or anon (verified against production 2026-09-02), and the two graph helpers are SECURITY INVOKER so RLS applies to them normally. anon holds zero execute on every one of these. A person completing a step they are looking at is the only client-reachable door into the engine, and it is guarded from inside. CORRECTED 2026-09-09: this reason originally also named workflow_run_start as ungranted-to-authenticated. That was accurate for the 6-arg internal bridge overload (workflow_run_start(uuid,uuid,text,text,uuid,jsonb), still postgres/service_role only) but a separate 3-arg overload — workflow_run_start(p_definition_id uuid, p_subject_type text, p_subject_id uuid) — was added afterward as the deliberate browser entry point ("Start a run") and IS granted to authenticated. It is allowlisted in its own rule below rather than folded in here, because its own SECURITY DEFINER body carries its own tenant/activation checks and deserves its own justification.

notes.workflow_run_step_complete(p_step_id uui: SECURITY DEFINER because settling a step advances the run, and the branch rule and loop bounds must be applied in exactly one place (workflow_run_advance) which the caller may not execute directly. It does its own tenant check, written to FAIL CLOSED: `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM (SELECT auth_tenant_id() AS t) q WHERE q.t = v_tenant)` rather than `v_tenant NOT IN (...)`, because NOT IN yields NULL when the subquery yields NULL, an IF on NULL takes the ELSE branch, and the guard silently never fires — the exact shape this estate has shipped open before. is_platform_developer() is wrapped in coalesce(...,false) for the same reason: it returns NULL rather than false for a caller with no profile row. auth.uid() IS NULL means a server-side caller (service_role, trigger, or definer chain) already trusted upstream. The row is locked FOR UPDATE before the check, so the tenant cannot be changed under it, and completing an already-settled step is idempotent rather than an error.

rules.review: Re-justify if any further function in this bridge is granted to authenticated. The security property here is that there is exactly one guarded entry point; a second grant would move the guarantee from 'checked in one place' to 'checked in each place', which is the state this pattern exists to avoid.

objects: workflow_run_start(p_definition_id uuid, p_subject_type text, p_subject_id uuid)
rules.reason: Two overloads of workflow_run_start exist live, and only one is this finding. workflow_run_start(uuid,uuid,text,text,uuid,jsonb) (6-arg internal bridge) is postgres=EXECUTE, service_role=EXECUTE only — not this finding, not touched by this rule. workflow_run_start(uuid,text,uuid) (this 3-arg overload) is postgres, service_role, authenticated=EXECUTE, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path=public, pg_temp, and is the validated BROWSER entry point: crm7 src/lib/workflows/runService.ts:131 (supabase.rpc('workflow_run_start', {p_definition_id, p_subject_type, p_subject_id})), the 'Start a run' action on /workflows. Its body (read from the live pg_get_functiondef, 2026-09-09): a required-args check, then acting_scope_tenant_id() (raises 42501 when the caller has none), then the definition must be is_enabled in workflow_definition_activations for that tenant (42501 otherwise), then the placements subject must belong to the tenant (42501 otherwise), then it delegates to the 6-arg overload with started_via='manual'. A negative caller was proven 2026-09-09: an outsider account gets 42501, not a run. Per bsuite-rls-authz-red-team, a validated SECURITY DEFINER entry point with a pinned search_path and tenant/activation checks before it does anything is the sanctioned pattern for a client-reachable definer function, not a gap — revoking authenticated here would not harden anything, it would break the visual 'Start a run' journey the function exists to serve. RESIDUAL, hardening tracked, not this lane: the 3-arg overload's subject-ownership check is written only for the placements table today; a forward BSU migration will generalise it to a tenant_id ownership check for any subject table referenced by workflow_definition_activations, and fail closed for a subject type it does not recognise rather than silently passing.
rules.review: Re-justify if the generic subject-ownership hardening migration lands without this rule being re-read against its new body, or if a third overload of workflow_run_start appears.

objects: team_invitation_seat_available(p_team_id uuid, p_tenant_id uuid, p_user_id uuid)
rules.reason:
The RLS predicate added by business-suite-unified migration 20261201010300_recover_team_invitation_capacity_lock (applied to production), which replaced a team_invitations INSERT policy that queried team_invitations from inside its own WITH CHECK and so recursed under RLS.

This is the ESTABLISHED ACCEPTED CLASS on this list: RLS PREDICATES. team_invitations_admin_insert (FOR INSERT TO authenticated) calls it in WITH CHECK, and a policy expression is evaluated as the querying role, so revoking EXECUTE from authenticated would not narrow who can invite; it would fail every direct invitation insert. SECURITY DEFINER is what lets the predicate count team_invitations without re-entering that table's own policies.

VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-16 against the production catalog (SELECT only):
  * SECURITY DEFINER, VOLATILE, search_path pinned to 'public, pg_temp'.
  * proacl {postgres, service_role, authenticated}=X; has_function_privilege('anon', ...) = FALSE.
  * The live body is the migration's body exactly (908 bytes; whitespace-normalised md5 identical to the file).
  * Referenced by exactly ONE policy (public.team_invitations team_invitations_admin_insert) and by no other function.

It cannot be pointed at anyone else. It returns FALSE, before taking any lock or reading any row, unless p_user_id IS auth.uid(), the caller is_team_admin of p_team_id, and p_tenant_id is one of the caller's own auth_tenant_id() tenants. Only then does it take the per-tenant advisory transaction lock (lock_team_seat_capacity, which authenticated cannot execute) and return one BOOLEAN: whether members plus live pending invitations are below the tenant's latest subscription seat_count. No row data leaves the function.
rules.review: Re-justify if the signature changes (objects match by full signature), if any policy other than team_invitations_admin_insert or any function starts calling it, or if the early-return checks on auth.uid(), is_team_admin and auth_tenant_id() are ever loosened.
